topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: We stood in the foyer, the air thick with silence and the lingering scent of her lavender soap. This house, once filled with the warmth of her laughter and the clatter of her old silverware, now echoed with the finality of something lost. Every wall, every creak of the floorboards, seemed to whisper her name, a gentle reproach. The will had been read, and now this place was ours. But it felt wrong, as if we were intruding on a memory that didn’t belong to us. I kept thinking about the times she’d shared stories of this house, how it held more than just bricks and mortar—it was the vessel of her life. I wished I could turn back the clock, return it to her. Instead, we stood there, stewing in the hush, the weight of her absence pressing down on us.
